pr_body:
The ssl_old_test has not been fully converted to the test framework but it still reuses some test framework utilities. Notably it was creating it's own copy of the global bio_err object directly (which is normally created and owned by the test framework). This causes a problem because ever since commit 2fa9044 access to the bio_err object is controlled by a lock. Since ssl_old_test was circumventing the normal creation and destruction of bio_err, the lock was not being created resulting in a crash under certain error conditions.

We fix this by creating and destroying the bio_err object using the test framework functions designed for that purpose.

Fixes #23184

issue_context.title: Crash in "test\ssl_old_test.exe"
issue_context.body:
Running the tests on Win-10 (MSVC, x64 version), I note several crashes in `CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock()` due
to a missing call to `CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new()`. Assuming via `test/recipes/80-test_ssl_old.t` only (?).

When running this manually:
```
cd test\recipes
..\ssl_old_test.exe -s_key ..\..\certs\ee-key.pem -s_cert certU.ss -c_key ..\..\certs\ee-key.pem -c_cert certU.ss ^
-config ..\..\default-and-legacy.cnf -provider default -provider legacy -bio_pair
Warning: unknown compression not supported
Available compression methods:  zlib compression:1
```
I get a crash and this call-stack from WinDbg
```
ntdll!RtlAcquireSRWLockExclusive+0x10
ssl_old_test!CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(void * lock = 0x00000000`00000000)+0x18
ssl_old_test!test_vprintf_stderr(char * fmt = 0x00007ff6`1eeabcc0 "Error loading config from file %s.", char * ap = 0x00000070`a4cff9b8 ""???")+0x25
ssl_old_test!opt_printf_stderr(char * fmt = 0x00007ff6`1eeabcc0 "Error loading config from file %s.")+0x2b
ssl_old_test!test_get_libctx(struct ossl_lib_ctx_st ** libctx = 0x00000070`a4cffac8, struct ossl_provider_st ** default_null_prov = 0x00000070`a4cffb08, char * config_file = 0x000001ea`79b48f22 "..\..\default-and-legacy.cnf", struct ossl_provider_st ** provider = 0x00000070`a4cffb10, char * module_name = 0x000001ea`79b48f5b "legacy")+0xcb
ssl_old_test!main(int argc = 0n0, char ** argv = 0x000001ea`79b48ea0)+0x16fd
ssl_old_test!__scrt_common_main_seh(void)+0x10c
KERNEL32!BaseThreadInitThunk+0x14
ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart+0x21
```
A NULL-ptr reference (`rcx` == 0):
```
ntdll!RtlAcquireSRWLockExclusive+0x10:
00007ff9`bcbf90b0 f0480fba2900    lock bts qword ptr [rcx],0 ds:00000000`00000000=????????????????
```

But I fail to see where this `CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_new()` should be made. I'd assume it's the responsibility of 
`test_vprintf_stderr()` to setup it's own locks. It's not in the case in `ssl_old_test.exe`.  So trying this:
```diff
--- a/test/ssl_old_test.c 2023-11-02 13:26:42
+++ b/test/ssl_old_test.c 2024-01-03 07:37:26
@@ -945,6 +945,8 @@
     verbose = 0;
     debug = 0;

+    test_open_streams();
+
     bio_err = BIO_new_fp(stderr, BIO_NOCLOSE | BIO_FP_TEXT);
     bio_stdout = BIO_new_fp(stdout, BIO_NOCLOSE | BIO_FP_TEXT);
```

the crash is gone (!?)
comments: Which OpenSSL version do you seen this on?

> Which OpenSSL version do you seen this on?

The very latest; built from yesterdays `git master`. From `VERSION.dat`:
```
MAJOR=3
MINOR=3
PATCH=0
PRE_RELEASE_TAG=dev
BUILD_METADATA=
RELEASE_DATE=""
SHLIB_VERSION=3
```

Hmmm. ssl_old_test is unlike almost all the other tests in its structure. Almost all the other tests inherit their `main` function from the test framework (`test/testutil/main.c`). The `main` in that file explicitly calls `test_open_streams()` as its first call to ensure the lock is created. But `ssl_old_test` has its own main function and isn't based on the test framework, in spite of reusing various test framework utilities.

I guess the reason this hasn't been noticed before is because normally errors don't occur at this point in the process and so we never attempt to get the lock. But I see in your stack trace that we are printing an error related to the config file - so some environmental issue has triggered this.

>  - so some environmental issue has triggered this.

Undoubtedly. But a crash!!? And why does it use it's own `main()`?

> And why does it use it's own main()?

Legacy reasons. This test has existed for a long time - since before the current test framework existed (which was introduced in 1.1.0). I assume that when all the other tests were converted to the current framework, this one was only partially done. Probably because it was considered "too hard".

Ah! It seems that the io lock concept was only relatively recently introduced (in 2fa9044298).

The underlying bug has been there for some while I think. But prior to the above commit it didn't cause a crash. The failure of `ssl_old_test` to call `test_open_streams` means that the BIO's do not get created. But if you call `BIO_write` with a NULL BIO, it does not cause a crash (it just fails). So previously, if `ssl_old_test` failed in this way then it would just fail silently without printing the error message that it was trying to print. Now, ever since 2fa9044298, we try to get a lock and don't check for NULL so it crashes.
Ok, good. I assume a fix is imminent.

> Ok, good. I assume a fix is imminent.

Working on it now.

> The failure of ssl_old_test to call test_open_streams means that the BIO's do not get created. 

It turns out that is not entirely correct. `ssl_old_test` does something fairly dubious and creates its own `bio_err` object (which is a global and is declared in `test/testutil/main.c`). It really shouldn't do that - I will correct it in my upcoming fix.

review_comments: Oops. This inadvertently changes EXIT_SUCCESS to EXIT_FAILURE. It's not entirely clear which is more appropriate here....but I did not mean to change this, so fixup coming.

I've noticed that but I assumed we do not use the `-F` option in our test recipes and it looks like an error-exit anyway. Perhaps it was meaningful as a test-skip kind of action at 1.0.2 FIPS module times.
